entries.english:
83. King Frederick’s safe-conduct for the Bohemian deputies (August 1448). Register no. 2472.

King Frederick grants a royal safe-conduct to the Bohemian nobles and representatives of Prague and other towns and communities travelling to a general diet to be held in Vienna on the feast of St Giles. The meeting, convened by the king and the cardinal legate John, is intended for negotiations concerning the welfare and peaceful condition of the Kingdom of Bohemia and the king’s principalities and domains. The safe-conduct covers the named nobles and envoys, their retinues, servants, and subjects, up to 1,000 horses and an equal number of persons, through the king’s lands and jurisdictions, for travel to Vienna, residence there, and their return or onward journey, until the coming feast of St Gall. The king promises that the protection will be faithfully observed.

If anyone in either party’s retinue causes damage, obstruction, or insult, this will not invalidate the safe-conduct; the parties must provide due redress. The king commands all his subjects to let the envoys and their companions travel, remain, and return in peace, without hindrance, and to show them every honor and favor. The instrument is dated 28 September 1448.
